arXiv:2610.16018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement witnesses are a key instrument in determining the entanglement of unknown bipartite qubit systems without requiring a full tomography. Riccardi et al. (2020) proposed a set of two-qubit witnesses, denoted W³, which require a set of local measurements in three bases. arXiv:2610.17058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires orchestrating millions of operations continuously across a tightly coupled classical-quantum control stack. arXiv:2610.16267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate Rényi divergences. arXiv:2610.17137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodically driven quantum systems exhibit a wide range of complex dynamics, including chaos. Yet, at special parameter values, their evolution can recur exactly. Several quantum protocols have recently been proposed that exploit exact Floquet recurrences to demonstrate genuine quantum advantage. Such recurrences can be studied through the arithmetic structure of the Floquet unitary. In this work, we establish a necessary and sufficient arithmetic criterion for exact recurrence and determine the minimal recurrence period when one exists. Because recurrence is a global property of the unitary, it holds for every initial state. arXiv:2610.15021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum science and engineering increasingly target the exploitation and control of large-scale dynamical systems. item.title: Quantitative upper bounds for certain quantum channel divergences
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Morgan Jones
arXiv:2610.16270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that completely positive maps can be decomposed into sums of submaps which are close in completely bounded trace norm but as far apart as possible in terms of geometric channel fidelity. We then show that this kind of behavior extends to a large class of quantum channel divergences. We construct quantitative norm estimates for quantum channel divergences in terms of the Arveson-Radon-Nikodym theorem.

item.title: Quantum circuit representation and incomplete Bell measurements in Compton scattering
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Wei Xie, Yu-Chen Guo, Shuang Li, Ji-Chong Yang
arXiv:2610.15526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate massless tree-level Compton scattering as an effective two-qubit operation on electron and photon helicities. In the Bell basis, the scattering map separates into two parity sectors and admits a simple quantum circuit representation with one nonunitary filter. After Kraus normalization, this filter defines an unsharp incomplete Bell measurement that distinguishes the two Bell-parity sectors but not the relative Bell label within each sector. We further show that the incomplete measurement alone does not surpass the classical teleportation threshold, whereas a subsequent complete Bell-basis readout enables unit conditional teleportation fidelity.

High-throughput stabilizer simulators, such as Stim, are the de facto tools for this regime. However, these simulators typically support only Clifford gates and stochastic Pauli noise. As a result, more realistic device noise models-such as coherent control errors and thermal relaxation-are often approximated using Pauli Twirling. This replacement offers speed but can introduce inaccuracies. item.title: Separability criteria and lower bounds of entanglement via realignment
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yuhang Xie, Yanjun Chu, Shao-Ming Fei
arXiv:2610.15664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection and quantification of quantum entanglement are central problems in quantum information science. Based on the realignment of density matrices and the vectorization of reduced density matrices, we construct a family of enhanced separability criteria for bipartite and multipartite quantum systems. Our criteria recover the previously proposed realignment-based criteria as special cases and detect more entanglement than the earlier ones. Moreover, we derive tighter lower bounds for the concurrence and the convex-roof extended negativity, criteria for detecting the genuine tripartite entanglement, and lower bounds on genuine-multipartite-entanglement concurrence. The advantages of our results are demonstrated with detailed examples.

item.description:
📚 Quantum Science and Technology
👤 Sinan Pehlivanoglu, Srinivasan Iyengar and Amr Sabry
Classical simulation of quantum circuits is expensive for two distinct reasons. The obvious one is state-space size: an -qubit system requires exponentially many amplitudes. The less obvious one is interference: useful output distributions emerge only after many computational histories have been coherently combined at common endpoints, and this aggregation step is itself a substantial source of cost. We introduce statistical interference sampling, a framework that makes this second bottleneck explicit by treating endpoint interference as a separately schedulable computation. item.title: Pathfinder-BP: A Low-Latency Recursive Decoder for Topological Codes
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Stefano Tinelli, Francisco Lázaro, Francisco García Herrero
arXiv:2610.16375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose Pathfinder-BP, a recursive decoder for topological quantum codes that combines belief propagation with controlled bit-flipping. An initial BP pass identifies and permanently fixes high-confidence errors. Upon convergence failure, the decoder recursively explores alternative error patterns by tentatively flipping low-confidence variables. On surface codes, Pathfinder-BP achieves a noise threshold and logical error rate comparable to minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM). A crucial advantage of Pathfinder-BP is its highly parallelizable structure, which yields a worst-case decoding latency quasi-linear in the code distance, making it a suitable candidate for low-latency hardware implementation.

👤 Evan Zhang, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Yu-Xin Wang, Ali Fahimniya, Daniel J. Spencer, Sean R. Muleady, Mohammad Hafezi, Andrew M. Childs, Alexey V. Gorshkov
arXiv:2610.17176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether controlled motion of a quantum sensor offers a metrological advantage in a field-detection task.
